title: Sweet Sorceress
intro: Identity and packaging for a small US confectioner making premium, fully handmade chocolate-covered dragée. A little bit of magic, built to be assembled at a kitchen table.
brief: Everything at Sweet Sorceress was made by hand, including the packaging, so the brand needed a system a handful of people could put together quickly without driving up costs. That meant universal packaging they could buy in bulk and assemble themselves, labels that complied with US food retail regulations, and a range of more than twenty flavour combinations. On top of the practical side, the owner wanted the brand to feel whimsical: like you're getting something a little magical when you treat yourself.
did: Developed together with Monica Ramilison. The identity is built around a hand-drawn cauldron overflowing with dragée, and slightly crooked lettering, to feel personal and a little playful instead of polished and corporate.

For the packaging the client chose to work with stock clear jars, which they could buy in bulk and let the colour of the dragée itself do part of the work. Everything else lives on gloss stick-on labels: quick to apply by hand, and they won't stain from chocolate-covered fingers. A matching lid sticker carries the logo, and for assortments, a plain kraft bag with a seal keeps the same character on an even smaller budget.

Each of the twenty-plus flavours has its own vector illustration of its main ingredients, from yuzu and matcha to cranberries and wild berries, so the label tells you what's inside at a glance. The layouts make room for the US nutrition panel, recycling marks and barcode without crowding out the fun part.
